then.text: Rain's coming. It always is. Pop back when the Enclosure's gone. Or when it's stopped raining. We'll be waiting a while.

else.text: Ha! You made it to Cardiff in one piece! Dry, too, which is frankly suspicious.
Rhys. Storm Stone. I play second row on Saturdays and I'm the one who gets rained on the rest of the week.
Right then. Forwards up front, backs out wide, and nobody drops the ball. Kick off!
The Storm Stone. Gale, gust and a good bit of drizzle. It's a lovely old thing. It's been in a drawer with my gumshield.
Your phone buzzes. Professor Garside, who sounds as if she is running.
{player}! The Storm Stone! That's four! Anwen rang. She says the stones are singing in tune.
The red dragon is awake and curious, so do pop back to Dinas Emrys when you've a spare hour. She'd like to meet whoever did all this.
But the next hum is east. Avebury and Stonehenge are both going, I can hear them down the phone line. Both at once. Like a pair of very old fridges.
Glastonbury is the loudest, though, so Glastonbury first. Cross the Severn to Bath, then over the Mendips. The road leaves Cardiff on the east side, past the docks.
The Keeper there is called Morwen. She takes visitors seriously and tea more seriously still. And mind the Enclosure. Their English Director is a Sir Rupert Ashcombe. Panama hat. Hates a loose end.
I'll ring again when you've the next Stone. Take biscuits. The Severn Bridge has a toll in both directions, and the toll is boredom.
The way east is open. Across the Severn lie Bath, the Mendips and Glastonbury.
